answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying one vote to locked collateral rather than to an address. Each agent contributes to a lagoon of stake anchored by a basalt ledger that no participant can rewrite, and distinct peers attest to each identity. Rewards grow with the square root of stake, so splitting one wallet into a hundred adds only a small delta to income while multiplying the capital an attacker must lock. Fake personas therefore cost real funds and pay almost nothing.
